rationale: A confidential-analysis user requests an explicit project-level safeguard against accidental public Git publication, including handoff to inexperienced collaborators. Removing remotes or shadowing wrapper functions is insufficient for the requested workflow. Discussion proposes an executable pre-push hook returning exit 1, compatible with archive-based handoff, while recognizing that hooks are not propagated by ordinary Git cloning. Maintainers later report implementation and availability in release 1.2.0 after raising Windows compatibility concerns.
scope_note: This is a preventive safeguard request, not an observed data breach. The participants distinguish public exposure from authorized private remotes and accidental action from malicious bypass. Release availability is reported, not independently executed. The implementation comment names wflow_git_push whereas the earlier proposal names wflow_start; do not silently resolve this API inconsistency. linked_1 repeats the same issue and comments rather than providing independent evidence.
provisional_concepts: Preventing accidental publication of confidential project outputs
Usable privacy safeguards for collaborative handoff

original_record.rationale: Spartacus develops persistent, purpose-specific anonymous consent choices with a reopenable dialog, bulk allow/reject, version-aware prompting and language-preserving state. The linked 18-commit patch implements localStorage and request/response consent headers, transfers granted optional consents after registration, distinguishes existing account preferences on login, and allows configured required consents to remain enabled. Banner dismissal is separate from giving consent. Later patches match consent to template identifiers, exclude required entries from bulk withdrawal, and serialize account operations. The test helper explicitly acknowledges stale responses can overwrite newly changed anonymous state.
original_record.scope_note: All supplied text and all 18 patches read. Tests inspected, not executed; checklist completion is a reported outcome, not independent assurance. Defaults specify no required consents; configuring a mandatory purpose is not proof of valid legal consent. Feature-level 1.3 gates the new behavior. The linked token-storage issue distinguishes consent to persistence from marketing; no claim of universal downstream tracking enforcement. Later user-store error report does not establish failure in every installation. Embedded external images were not inspected; interpretation rests on supplied text and code.
provisional_concepts: Persistent and context-consistent consent management

rationale: Matomo users need reversible cookie consent without reloading a single-page application. Disabling cookies does not stop fingerprint-based tracking; switching state initially fragments visits and visitor identity. The supplied patch sequence adds re-enabling, attribution-cookie setup, an optional ping and server visitor-ID updates, then distinguishes requireCookieConsent/setCookieConsentGiven/rememberCookieConsentGiven/forgetCookieConsentGiven from tracking consent. Consent persistence, scope and revocation must match the operation actually permitted.
scope_note: All supplied discussion, source snapshots, patch sequences and documentation read, with exact duplicate lines/segments cross-referenced in record94_exact_duplicates.json and record94_segment_duplicates.json. PR16113 patch07 removes cookie state from all fingerprints, but patch08 restricts the constant-zero handling to IE; do not describe the interim universal removal as final. Patch13 adds a ping, patch16 removes sending it, patch19 restores it with visitor-ID update. PR16178 documents distinct consent APIs; its rememberConsentGiven implementation accepts one parameter although forgetUserOptOut passes a second false flag, so the supplied code does not establish the claimed no-cookie opt-in behavior in every path. Comments incorrectly implying cookie-free tracking always needs no consent are not legal conclusions. Documentation says forever while code defaults to 30 years; release labels differ between changelog3.13.7 and docs3.14.0. Tests and screenshots were not executed/visually checked.
provisional_concepts: Separate and reversible consent for cookies and tracking

evidence.quote: Is there a way to turn cookies back on?

rationale: Sails authentication breaks when IE accepts transient browser-session cookies but blocks persistent first-party cookies: repeated new sessions cause CSRF mismatch. provisional_concepts: Adapting essential session lifetime to browser privacy restrictions

rationale: Firestore users request clearing persisted documents at logout or on explicit request, alongside separate demands to control cache growth and pending writes. Maintainers explain that same-OS-account persistence does not isolate people, and clearing on logout cannot cover crashes or forgotten logout. Direct partial IndexedDB deletion can invalidate resume tokens and corrupt synchronization. Later comments report GC in 5.7.0 and clearPersistence in 6.2.0. The linked iOS five-patch series implements reference-based LRU infrastructure that retains active targets and pending mutations, with restart-metadata fixes; it is not proof of secure erasure on web.
scope_note: All supplied text read, including all five linked_3 iOS patches. Distinguish clearing API, automatic cache eviction, and security isolation. Related WKWebView WAL growth report identifies a platform-specific problem; closing the Firebase instance and waiting is reported as a workaround, not deletion of cached documents. No execution or forensic erasure verification.
provisional_concepts: Removing retained local data without overstating user isolation
